newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - HRW YIELDS SEEN HIGH.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - HRW YIELDS SEEN HIGH.

text.p: Hard red winter wheat yields in Montana were coming in higher than average but few farmers were willing to sell, several grain dealers said.
"It looks really good," an eastern Montana dealer said. "We're getting 50 to 60 bushels per acre with protein averaging 12 to 12-1/2 percent. We usually get 30 to 35 bushels per acre."
Further west, yields were coming in closer to 40 or 50 bushels per acre with proteins mostly around 12 percent, another Montana dealer said.
Farmers were reluctant to part with the grain.
"I talked to a (merchandiser) today who said the elevator is full and he doesn't own a bushel," the dealer said. "All these guys are storing it."
Bids for hard red winter and spring wheat were mostly higher on Thursday, in line with gains in futures.
